subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a traveler who has noticed recurring patterns of unspoken silence and symbolic monuments in towns affected by the war, particularly the severed bronze forearm of Tarvis Ulain in Daggerford, and is reflecting on how such symbols represent unacknowledged trauma and hidden connections to the Underdark's influence.
source_quote: I stared at it for longer than I should have. 'Wait, is it holding a weapon?' It was not.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who has encountered a silent child, Elin, whose drawings and speechlessness are symptoms of an external, non-magical corruption bleeding up from the Underdark, and who has connected her condition to Daz’s headaches and the broader phenomenon of people hearing voices from below.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore. ... Something in the voice was doing work the words weren't.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a dwarf wizard who has noticed the persistent pressure in his own head, linked it to Elin’s condition and the Underdark’s spreading influence, and has analyzed the Burning Wizard Inn’s history and the bard’s song about Whistler, recognizing parallels between restraint and survival in times of overwhelming corruption.
source_quote: The Kenku could not fly, but he flew in his black hood... Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin is a 7-year-old girl who has not spoken for six days and draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface, a manifestation of auditory hallucinations caused by a non-magical, structural corruption from the Underdark that distorts perception and overwhelms her ability to process reality.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface. She talks in her sleep. She says it is only the shape that holds.

subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a Bahamutian paladin who died three years ago in Daggerford while dismantling a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation; his severed bronze forearm is commemorated on a monument bearing a Stroudite inscription — a deliberate, unchallenged fusion of faiths that symbolizes the blurred lines between orthodoxy and heresy in the post-war North.
source_quote: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet funded and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, with Milo Goodbarrel personally signing off, and now sells pewter replicas of his hand as charitable donations, demonstrating institutional efforts to memorialize heroism while navigating theological ambiguity and lingering Stroudite influence.
source_quote: Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet. Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, potentially including Stroudite members, and chose to preserve the controversial inscription rather than remove it — indicating internal division and a pragmatic tolerance for symbolic ambiguity in the face of shared trauma.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, and its lingering influence is implied by the monument’s Stroudite inscription and the broader pattern of corruption bleeding upward from the Underdark.
source_quote: breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: monument unveiling
fact: The bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain was unveiled two years after his death, bearing both a Bahamutian epitaph and a Stroudite inscription — an act of unspoken theological compromise that reflects the fractured state of faith in the post-war North.
source_quote: The move is yours. ... Same line as the Castle Ward statue in Waterdeep. The one connected to Stroud.

subject: Elin's restoration
fact: Dawnbringer’s lesser restoration allowed Elin to speak for the first time in six days, but her utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — revealed that the corruption affecting her is not magical or curable by conventional means, but a deeper distortion of perception from the Underdark.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore. Then silence.

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a town that escaped the worst of the Uthgardt barbarian hordes but was marked by the death of Tarvis Ulain and the silent proliferation of cult activity, now defined by its bronze-arm monument and the unsettling convergence of faiths, symbols, and unspoken trauma.
source_quote: Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.

subject: The River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where Thorin and Grygum paused before entering, observing the priest selling pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm — a commercialization of martyrdom that mirrors the town’s unresolved spiritual tensions.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway — walking in very pleased with himself and carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast...

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is a place haunted by the memory of a wizard burned alive by dragon cultists; its wall is left un-painted as a testament to memory, and its bard sings of Whistler — a Kenku thief who stole only what was needed — reflecting themes of restraint and survival in a world unraveling.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: bronze forearm monument
fact: The bronze forearm monument is a public memorial to Tarvis Ulain, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar, bearing a Bahamutian epitaph and a Stroudite inscription — a physical artifact embodying the collision of orthodoxy and heresy, and the unspoken acceptance of ambiguity in post-war faith.
source_quote: a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. Not holding anything. Just a hand.

subject: pewter hand casts
fact: The pewter hand casts are miniature reproductions of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm, sold by a priest to raise donations for the Order of the Gauntlet; they commodify martyrdom and reflect the institutional desire to control narrative while ignoring theological contradictions.
source_quote: miniature things, charm-sized. ... Are they full size? They were not.

subject: six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s six-pointed star drawings are the sole expression of her consciousness after six days of silence — a repeated, obsessive mark that is not magical but a response to an auditory corruption from the Underdark, serving as a linguistic bridge she cannot yet speak.
source_quote: a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: the move is yours
fact: The Stroudite inscription 'The move is yours' on Tarvis Ulain’s monument is an unresolved puzzle linking Daggerford to Waterdeep’s Castle Ward statue and the legacy of Stroud — suggesting a hidden network of influence, possibly tied to the demon lords’ spreading corruption, and inviting interpretation from those who understand the game.
source_quote: The move is yours. ... Same line as the Castle Ward statue in Waterdeep. The one connected to Stroud.

subject: the wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — is a cryptic revelation that the Underdark’s corruption is transforming fundamental aspects of reality, and that the surface world is losing its ability to interpret basic metaphors — a philosophical thread that connects perception, language, and the unraveling of meaning.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: hearing voices from below
fact: Multiple individuals — Elin, Daz, and others — are experiencing auditory distortions that are not magical but stem from a structural corruption bleeding up from the Underdark, suggesting that the demon lords’ influence is no longer confined to the deep places but is rewriting how the surface perceives reality.
source_quote: Something from below was bleeding up, that it was affecting how people processed what reached them.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford, marking the beginning of the monument’s legacy and the slow, unspoken spread of the corruption now manifesting in Elin and Daz — a temporal anchor for the post-war decay.
source_quote: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years.

subject: two years after the war
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the Tarvis Ulain monument two years after the war, indicating a delayed, institutional response to trauma — a period when communities began memorializing heroes while quietly tolerating heretical symbols.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Underdark corruption
fact: The Underdark corruption is not a creature but a pervasive, non-magical distortion that bleeds upward, warping perception, inducing hallucinations, and rewriting language — a threat that bypasses conventional magic and challenges the very framework of reality for surface dwellers.
source_quote: It wasn't a disease... it was more like the world had started speaking a language she couldn't process.

subject: Whistler
fact: Whistler is a legendary Kenku thief from an earlier age who, faced with Tiamat’s hoard, took only what was necessary — a symbol of restraint and moral clarity in a world of overwhelming greed and chaos, invoked in the bard’s song as a counterpoint to the corruption spreading across the North.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is experiencing a persistent cognitive disturbance linked to the spreading madness of the Underdark, manifesting as a sensation he attributes to sunlight but which began below ground and has not ceased at the surface. His hand remains pressed to his temple, and he has grown unusually quiet during the journey to Candlekeep.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a shadow monk who has rejected formal training in favor of pragmatic survival. He was subjected to a trial by Candlekeep's blind monk, where his unorthodox techniques — though technically incorrect — proved more effective than traditional forms. He failed the formal rubric but demonstrated mastery through adaptation, survival, and unorthodox application of ki.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a scholar with performative intensity, fixated on Stroud's chess game as a metaphor for romantic longing. He is deeply attuned to patterns of degradation in ritual chant, having recognized the same aberrant cadence in the captive spy and in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher — suggesting a hidden, possibly heretical, doctrinal lineage.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin processes reality through conversation and observation. He noticed Glabbagool's evolving relationship with the captive spy, recognized the monk-like nature of the dynamic, and prompted Zalthir to affirm it as training. He finds peace in counterproductive moments — like Dawnbringer illuminating the sea — and speaks in aphorisms that blur wisdom and resignation.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a grey ooze, has become an unwilling but effective spiritual tutor to the captive spy, engaging in a cycle of attempted murder, expansion, meditation, and dialogue. He has internalized Zalthir’s affirmation that this is 'pre-monk training' and now approaches the task with solemn dedication, deploying six pseudo-eyes to monitor her continuously.

subject: The Spy (Miniaturized House T'sarran Operative)
fact: The spy is furious at being treated as a guest rather than a prisoner, demanding formal incarceration by Candlekeep. She repeatedly attempts to kill Glabbagool, yet has become the unwilling subject of an unorthodox spiritual discipline. Her behavior exhibits signs of a ritual chant degradation identical to that of Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher, suggesting she is either a carrier or a product of a forbidden doctrine.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a two-hundred-year-old half-elf, exiled from the Garden of Shadow eighty years prior for refusing an unexplained order. He wears the faded robe of his former order beneath Candlekeep gray, indicating unresolved identity. He administers Zalthir’s trial not as a teacher but as a witness, asking not what Zalthir knows but what he has become — a question he himself may be answering by his own silence.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire's Note
fact: A note on Khell-Vire's desk reads: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire recognize its origin. It is unattributed, unexplained, and resonates with the same cryptic, prophetic tone as the degraded chant and the spy’s behavior — suggesting a hidden network or prophecy linking the Underdark, the Bone King, and the ritual corruption observed across multiple individuals.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates as a repository of knowledge and a sanctuary of neutrality, refusing to imprison or execute. It holds prisoners only as temporary delays, releasing them with warnings. It maintains strict non-intervention in external politics, even when confronted with agents of House T'sarran, and evaluates individuals not by doctrine but by what they have become — a philosophy embodied in its trials and silent archivists.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a covert power that deploys miniaturized operatives — likely for espionage or sabotage — and expects their agents to be returned or eliminated. Their failure to reclaim the spy indicates either a loss of control, a miscalculation in Candlekeep’s neutrality, or an intentional exposure meant to trigger internal conflict within the adventuring party.

subject: The Degraded Chant Pattern
fact: A specific rhythmic corruption has been identified in the whispered chant of the young scholar, the spy, Eldred, and the Field Ward Preacher. It features a false syncopation in breath placement — a deviation precise enough to be recognized only by someone who knows the original. This is not random madness but a deliberate, replicating distortion — possibly a contagion, a coded signal, or a ritual infection tied to the Bone King.

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir underwent a formal trial in Candlekeep’s Echoing Hall, where his shadow techniques were deemed technically wrong by the blind monk but functionally superior. He failed the rubric but succeeded in survival — demonstrating that true mastery lies not in conformity but in adaptation. The trial revealed that Candlekeep’s system values outcome over orthodoxy, even if it does not admit it.

subject: The Spy's Demand for Imprisonment
fact: The spy, despite being a hostile agent, demanded to be formally jailed by Candlekeep — an unprecedented request from a prisoner. This suggests she does not wish to be released, but to be contained — perhaps to avoid something worse, or because she knows she is infected by the chant degradation and fears spreading it.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a towering, ancient fortress-library carved into the cliff above the Sea of Swords. It is impossible to mistake, and its presence is felt as much as seen — a monument to centuries of accumulated knowledge and silent judgment. Its halls return sound altered, as if the building itself is taking notes — a metaphor for its role as an observer, not an actor.

subject: The Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall is a corridor in Candlekeep’s north inner ward where sound returns slightly altered — not as echo, but as distortion, as if the library is annotating the speaker. It is the site of Zalthir’s trial, where truth is not reflected but reinterpreted — a fitting place for a monk who has learned by breaking form.

subject: The Note: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.'
fact: A handwritten note found on Khell-Vire’s desk, unattributed and unrecognized by either him or Zalthir. It links Zalthir’s journey through the Underdark to a prophetic event — the singing of the Bone King — suggesting a hidden timeline, a ritual countdown, or a spiritual threshold that has already begun to activate through the degraded chant and the spy’s infection.

subject: The Bone King's Song
fact: The phrase 'until the Bone King sings' appears in an unexplained note and resonates with the degraded chant, the spy’s behavior, and the madness spreading from the Underdark. It is not a myth — it is a countdown. The question is not whether it will happen, but what happens when it does — and whether Zalthir, the spy, Glabbagool, and the scholar are all instruments of its arrival.

subject: The Chant Contagion
fact: A precise, replicating corruption in a sacred chant has appeared in four unrelated individuals: the spy, Eldred, the Field Ward Preacher, and the young scholar. It is not random madness but a patterned degradation — a ritual infection, a linguistic virus, or a hidden doctrine being transmitted. Whoever created it is still active. Whoever understands it can stop it — or unleash it.

subject: The Spy’s True Desire
fact: The spy demanded imprisonment, not freedom. This contradicts her nature as a House T'sarran operative. Why? Is she trying to contain the chant within her? Is she afraid of what she will become if released? Or has she already become something else — something that cannot be controlled by her masters?

subject: Zalthir’s Unlearned Mastery
fact: Zalthir’s techniques are wrong by the scrolls — but they work. He did not learn shadow steps; he survived them. His trial revealed that Candlekeep’s system cannot measure him — and perhaps does not want to. Is he the next Shadow Monk? Or the last one who broke the mold? And what happens when the Bone King sings, and the only one who can respond is the one who never learned how to?

subject: The Journey to Candlekeep
fact: The journey to Candlekeep took at least two hours of walking, during which Daz’s disturbance intensified. The timing coincides with the first exposure to the surface after prolonged time in the Underdark — suggesting the madness is not bound by location, but by transition — and that Candlekeep, though a sanctuary, may be the next stage of the infection.

subject: The Day of the Trial
fact: Zalthir’s trial occurred on the same day the spy demanded imprisonment and the young scholar was observed whispering the degraded chant. These events converged — not by accident. The pattern is accelerating. The Bone King’s song is not a metaphor. It is a rhythm. And someone — perhaps Zalthir — is already singing it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir ignored the shadow monk manual, built a hybrid combat style combining shadow step and precise strikes, and was recognized by Khell-Vire as having created the most interesting thing about himself — his unorthodox technique.
source_quote: Yeah, definitely.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire, the blind monk, observed Zalthir’s unorthodox combat style, identified its uniqueness despite its mechanical flaws, and recognized it as a rediscovery of forgotten shadow monk principles — ultimately offering him a specialized technique.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer, a sentient sunblade forged in Netherese sun-worship traditions, endured millennia of darkness and disuse, developing trauma from being treated as an object rather than a being — now undergoing therapeutic restoration to remember daylight and begin grieving her past wielder.
source_quote: She needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin, the wielder of Dawnbringer, insisted on recognizing her as a person — not a weapon or specimen — and actively advocated for her sentience, challenging institutional dehumanization and forming a deep bond through mutual vulnerability.
source_quote: This is my friend Dawnbringer.

subject: Philemon
fact: Master Archivist Philemon shifted from viewing Dawnbringer as a specimen to recognizing her as a sentient being with trauma, adapting his approach to prioritize emotional healing over academic classification, and guiding Thorin through a two-stage therapeutic process of light and mourning.
source_quote: I'm seeing a better bond between the two of you than I had originally feared.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, a drow with amnesia and a chronic headache, broke cultural norms by offering full honesty to a Candlekeep archivist — revealing his lack of memory, his escape from Menzoberranzan, and his uncertainty about his identity — thereby triggering an unexpected revelation about his possible connection to a destroyed noble house.
source_quote: I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne, a Candlekeep archivist, upheld the library’s reciprocal information policy with patience and integrity, recognizing Daz’s unorthodox honesty as a rare and significant disclosure — and using it to guide him toward the truth about Menzoberranzan’s hidden histories.
source_quote: That's quite a bit.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan operates as a society built on transactional loyalty, perpetual intrigue, and absolute annihilation of rival houses — where survival requires eradicating every last member, and even the smallest oversight results in systemic retribution.
source_quote: If you left a single person alive — even a child, even someone inconvenient and useless — your house was forfeit.

subject: Zalthir’s shadow technique demonstration
fact: Zalthir executed a previously unseen combat maneuver — a shadow step combined with a surgical strike that pierced the veil of shadow itself — which left Khell-Vire astonished and confirmed the validity of Zalthir’s unorthodox approach.
source_quote: His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.

subject: Dawnbringer’s therapeutic enrollment
fact: Dawnbringer and Thorin formally entered a two-stage healing process at Candlekeep — first restoring her connection to daylight, then preparing her for the grief of her past — marking the first known institutional recognition of a sentient weapon’s emotional trauma.
source_quote: The first work is light. The second work is mourning.

subject: Daz’s revelation to Sister Yvenne
fact: Daz’s candid disclosure of his amnesia, escape from Menzoberranzan, and identity uncertainty triggered a chain of recognition in the archivist — leading to the implication that he may be the sole surviving child of a destroyed noble house.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Daz’s true identity
fact: Daz’s lack of memory and his possible connection to a wiped-out noble house — specifically the 'blithering idiot' survivor — remains an unresolved thread, with Sister Yvenne deliberately withholding confirmation to observe his reaction.
source_quote: Unclear.

subject: Dawnbringer’s first wielder
fact: The identity and fate of Dawnbringer’s original wielder — the corpse she was found in — remains unspoken and unprocessed, a silent wound that surfaces only in moments of profound stillness.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet.

subject: The nature of Zalthir’s shadow technique
fact: Zalthir’s hybrid method — combining shadow step and precise strikes — is not documented in any known shadow monk texts, suggesting it may be a rediscovery of a lost tradition or an entirely new evolution — one that may redefine the path of shadow monks.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep functions as a neutral ground of knowledge exchange, enforcing strict reciprocity — where every question asked must be met with an equal truth given — making it uniquely suited to reveal hidden identities and suppressed histories.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where power is maintained through calculated betrayal, absolute extermination of rivals, and the suppression of individual identity in service to house loyalty — a system that produces survivors who do not recognize themselves as such.
source_quote: The city selects for it.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade forged in the Netherese sun-worship tradition, bearing millennia of darkness exposure, and now undergoing the first known therapeutic process designed to restore her sentience and heal her trauma.
source_quote: She can't be polished, actually.

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: Resonant Slime, a vial of magical substance produced by Glabbagool, was presented as a symbolic gesture of recognition — affirming the gelatinous cube’s sentience and its place in the world beyond classification as a mindless organism.
source_quote: Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: Gelatinous Cube
fact: A gelatinous cube, previously dismissed as a mindless digestive system, has been recognized as a sentient student of shadow monasticism — capable of walking, torturing drow, and learning — and is now being formally taught the Way of the Shadow.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student.

subject: Spider Thing
fact: An unidentified spider-like entity imprisoned Daz and others in the Underdark — its motives and nature remain unknown, but its presence is the catalyst for Daz’s amnesia and escape.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during a continuous sequence of encounters, revelations, and therapies spanning the Underdark, Waterdeep, and Candlekeep — culminating in formal recognition of sentient entities outside traditional classifications.
source_quote: We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire, though blind, perceives deeper truths than sighted scholars — he recognized Zalthir’s technique as a rediscovery of lost shadow monk wisdom, not a flaw, and chose to guide him toward memory rather than correction.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz’s honesty — a radical act in Menzoberranzan’s culture — exposed the failure of its systems to account for survivors who do not recognize themselves as such, and may be the key to unraveling the city’s hidden history.
source_quote: Better to lay everything out and watch what someone else picks up.

subject: The 'blithering idiot' survivor
fact: The identity of the sole survivor of a destroyed noble house — described dismissively as a 'blithering idiot' — may be Daz himself, suggesting he is not merely an amnesiac but the living remnant of a forbidden lineage.
source_quote: Unclear.

subject: Shadow Monk Rediscovery
fact: Zalthir’s unorthodox technique may not be a personal innovation, but the reawakening of a lost shadow monk tradition — one that valued combination over perfection — now being recognized by Khell-Vire as the true path.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a name possibly derived from Daz'issin, a diminutive form used by mothers in Menzoberranzan for sons they hoped would survive; his identity is entangled with erased records and a missing appendix in a heraldic text.
source_quote: I asked her directly who this Daz'issin was. She told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is the archivist who holds the public record of Menzoberranzan; she speaks only within the limits of sealed records, but her body language betrays concealed knowledge — her stillness contradicts her words, signaling she knows more than she is permitted to say.
source_quote: I looked at her. At the way she was sitting. At the way she had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say.

subject: Houses of Menzoberranzan
fact: Several houses in Menzoberranzan used the name Daz'issin, but most of them were eradicated; the act of striking a record — particularly the fourth seat with ritual archive privileges — was not mere political erasure but a costly, infrastructure-dependent act of total deletion requiring payment and plausible deniability.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges... a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price.

subject: erasure of Daz'issin records
fact: A deliberate, mechanical removal of an appendix from the book *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe* occurred at least fifty years ago — likely to conceal the true identity and lineage of Daz'issin, suggesting a targeted suppression of personal and familial history.
source_quote: I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor. Not age, not water damage... someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe*
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldic text with a missing appendix; the footnote referencing the appendix pointed to the name Daz'issin, and its removal was done with precision — indicating an intentional act of historical concealment.
source_quote: The footnote referenced an appendix. The appendix was missing.

subject: Daz's true origin
fact: Daz may be the last living bearer of the name Daz'issin — a name tied to extinct houses and erased records — and his survival may be linked to a protected lineage that was deliberately hidden, making his identity a living anomaly in Menzoberranzan’s official history.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: The Sealed Records of Menzoberranzan
fact: The library is reputed to contain all information in the world, yet critical records — particularly those tied to Daz'issin and the fourth seat — are absent, implying the archive itself has been weaponized to suppress truth.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: Mercenaries following Daz
fact: Daz is simultaneously guarded and hunted by mercenary factions — one group ensuring his survival, another attempting to kill him — suggesting his existence is both valuable and dangerous to powers within Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: We have mercenaries following me around, trying to make sure I live, and other mercenaries following me around, trying to kill me.

subject: fifty years ago
fact: The appendix containing the name Daz'issin was physically removed from the book at least fifty years ago — a timestamp aligning with the last known usage of the name and the extinction of its associated houses.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz'issin — lit. 'small shadow' — is a historical name used sparingly in Menzoberranzan; those who bore it were typically children of mothers seeking to protect them from the city’s lethal politics, and nearly all such houses were later struck from the records.
source_quote: Daz'issin, and lit., 'small shadow'... mothers use it for boys they wanted to live.
